title: Passing off vs trademark infringement - the difference that matters
p1:
Two businesses can look almost identical… but only one may have a trademark infringement problem.

Many people think copying a brand name or logo is always the same legal issue. Surprisingly, it isn't.
p2:
Trademark infringement usually happens when someone uses a protected trademark without permission and creates a risk of confusion. Passing off is different: it protects the reputation a business has built, even without a registered trademark.

A small business with a famous local name may still take action through passing off if another company tries to benefit from its goodwill.
p3:
The key difference is simple: trademark infringement focuses on registered rights, while passing off focuses on protecting customer trust and business reputation.

The practical takeaway? Registering a trademark gives stronger protection, but building a trusted brand can create valuable rights too.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a business name, logo, or product that felt like it was copying another brand? Do you think it was trademark infringement or passing off?
